title: RTX's Pratt & Whitney expands aerospace manufacturing capabilities in Kalisz

By bringing galvanic processing capability in-house, Pratt & Whitney is strengthening control over its manufacturing process, improving quality, reducing production lead times and providing additional capacity to meet industry demand. Galvanic facilities perform a key function in aerospace manufacturing, enabling the metallic plating of components for durability and corrosion resistance. The new facility combines an automated galvanizing process with high standards of environmental and safety controls. It reduces the use of hazardous chemicals and manages water usage with a closed-loop system that enables full neutralization of water and removal of waste material. # RTX's Pratt & Whitney expands aerospace manufacturing capabilities in Kalisz


November 27, 2026


- Share this article on Facebook
- Share this article on Twitter
- Share this article on LinkedIn
- Share this article via email


***Galvanic facility utilizes automation to reduce production lead times of key components for civil, commercial and military aircraft engines***


KALISZ, Poland (Nov. 27, 2026) — Pratt & Whitney, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, today announced the opening of a new galvanic facility at its Kalisz site, which manufactures precision components for multiple aircraft engine types serving civil, commercial and military operators around the world. By bringing galvanic processing capability in-house, Pratt & Whitney is strengthening control over its manufacturing process, improving quality, reducing production lead times and providing additional capacity to meet industry demand.


Galvanic facilities perform a key function in aerospace manufacturing, enabling the metallic plating of components for durability and corrosion resistance. The new facility combines an automated galvanizing process with high standards of environmental and safety controls. It reduces the use of hazardous chemicals and manages water usage with a closed-loop system that enables full neutralization of water and removal of waste material. The facility also features advanced safety systems, including gas detection systems, redundant safety sensors and safety gates that automatically stop production lines.


“The new galvanic facility marks another step in the development of Kalisz as a hub for advanced aerospace manufacturing and confirms Poland’s strategic importance to RTX,” said Wojciech Wasik, executive director, Board President, Pratt & Whitney Kalisz. “We are investing in technology, infrastructure and our employees’ skills, combining the highest standards of quality, safety and management of waste material.”


Operating since 1992, the Kalisz site is an important part of Pratt & Whitney’s global manufacturing network, producing components for multiple engine types, ranging from turboprops to military engines. Kalisz is also a center of excellence for geared components, including the fan drive gear system featured on the Pratt & Whitney GTF™ engines that power the latest generation of single-aisle aircraft such as the Airbus A220, A320neo and Embraer E2 families.


The project represents an investment of $12.5 million, which was supported by the Generator of Ecological Concepts, a joint program of Poland’s National Centre for Research and Development and the National Fund for Environmental Protection and Water Management.


Poland represents RTX's largest investment and employee base outside the United States, with more than 9,500 employees across its Collins Aerospace, Pratt & Whitney and Raytheon businesses in-country. More than 1,700 employees are based in Kalisz.


**About Pratt & Whitney**
Pratt & Whitney, an RTX business, is a world leader in the design, manufacture and service of aircraft engines and auxiliary power units for military, commercial and civil aviation customers. Since 1925, our engineers have pioneered the development of revolutionary aircraft propulsion technologies, and today we support more than 90,000 in-service engines through our global network of maintenance, repair and overhaul facilities.


**About RTX**
With more than 180,000 global employees, we push the limits of technology and science to redefine how we connect and protect our world. With industry-leading capabilities, we advance aviation, engineer integrated defence systems for operational success, and develop next-generation technology solutions and manufacturing to help global customers address their most critical challenges. The company, with 2025 sales of more than $88 billion, is headquartered in Arlington, Virginia.
